POST /tickets/{id}/status.abuse: Mass close/reopen with a token; every change checks base and ticket.close/create; no e-mail by itself.

POST /tickets/{id}/assignment.abuse: Reassignment noise; alert is opt-in (default false); base value required.

POST /tickets/{id}/claim.abuse: Reassignment noise; alert is opt-in (default false); base value required.

DELETE /tickets/{id}/assignment.abuse: Verb DELETE but nothing is deleted: it releases the assignment and logs `released`.

POST /tickets/{id}/transfer.reversible: partial (needs access in the target dept)
POST /tickets/{id}/transfer.abuse: Can move a ticket out of everyone's sight; requires ticket.transfer; alert opt-in; base value required.

POST /tickets/{id}/referrals.abuse: Grants another agent/team/dept visibility of the ticket; append-only, logged.

PATCH /tickets/{id}/fields/{name}.abuse: Field edits carry base; conflicting writes are 409; edits are logged as thread events.

PUT /tickets/{id}/forms.abuse: Field edits carry base; conflicting writes are 409; edits are logged as thread events.

POST /tickets/{id}/sla.abuse: `disable` and `clear_overdue` could hide an SLA breach: since PC-S2 (MSOLIS 2026-09-28) they need the department manager (or an administrator) on top of ticket.edit; `restart`, `extend`, `enable` stay with ticket.edit. Every operation leaves an internal SLA note plus the core events.

POST /tickets/{id}/replies.abuse: External e-mail. `notify` is REQUIRED (no default), claim and signature are explicit, `cc` accepts existing contacts only, PDF needs text, hourly budget (limit_mail_per_hour).

POST /tickets/{id}/notes.abuse: Internal only; alert default false; files must be the agent's own uploads; PDF needs explanatory text.

POST /tickets/{id}/notes/{entry}/files.abuse: Internal only; alert default false; files must be the agent's own uploads; PDF needs explanatory text.

PATCH /tickets/{id}/notes/{entry}.abuse: Internal notes only; edit = new linked entry, old one hidden and kept; never e-mails.

GET /documents/{uuid}.abuse: Only versions on tickets the agent can see; unknown/foreign uuid is 404.

POST /files.abuse: Storage/disk fill: per-file cap, type sniffing, hourly upload budget; the file is readable by its uploader only until attached.

GET /files/{hash}.abuse: Exfiltration surface: ACL = uploader, or an attachment on a ticket/task the agent can see; Range/inline/thumbnail run the same check first; CSP sandbox + nosniff.

POST /tickets/{id}/tasks.abuse: Creates internal work items; alert default false.

POST /tasks/{id}/notes.abuse: Task thread is internal; PDF rule applies.

POST /tasks/{id}/replies.abuse: Task thread is internal; PDF rule applies.

PATCH /tasks/{id}/notes/{entry}.abuse: Same edit rule as ticket notes.

GET /users.abuse: Directory reads: `user.dir` agents browse/page; the rest get autocomplete-sized (10), unpaged, min 3 chars, hourly lookup budget.

POST /users.abuse: Creates a portal identity; 409 candidates before creating; needs user.create.

GET /users/{id}.abuse: Reading one contact needs user.dir OR the contact is on a ticket the agent can see OR the agent created it (403 otherwise; id enumeration closed). Notes are append-only.

GET /users/{id}/tickets.abuse: Reading one contact needs user.dir OR the contact is on a ticket the agent can see OR the agent created it (403 otherwise; id enumeration closed). Notes are append-only.

GET /users/{id}/notes.abuse: Reading one contact needs user.dir OR the contact is on a ticket the agent can see OR the agent created it (403 otherwise; id enumeration closed). Notes are append-only.

POST /users/{id}/notes.abuse: Reading one contact needs user.dir OR the contact is on a ticket the agent can see OR the agent created it (403 otherwise; id enumeration closed). Notes are append-only.

PATCH /users/{id}.reversible: yes (base value; old value in the event)
PATCH /users/{id}.abuse: Name, phone and custom fields only, with user.edit + base value. The e-mail address is NOT editable (PC-S3, MSOLIS 2026-09-28): typed 422 `not_editable`.

PUT /users/{id}/organization.abuse: Organization membership drives org-shared ticket visibility in the portal; needs user.edit + base.

GET /organizations.abuse: Same directory rule as users (user.dir, or an organization on a visible ticket, or created by the agent).

GET /organizations/{id}.abuse: Same directory rule as users (user.dir, or an organization on a visible ticket, or created by the agent).

GET /organizations/{id}/members.abuse: Same directory rule as users (user.dir, or an organization on a visible ticket, or created by the agent).

GET /organizations/{id}/tickets.abuse: Same directory rule as users (user.dir, or an organization on a visible ticket, or created by the agent).

GET /organizations/{id}/fields.abuse: Same directory rule as users (user.dir, or an organization on a visible ticket, or created by the agent).

GET /organizations/{id}/notes.abuse: Same directory rule as users (user.dir, or an organization on a visible ticket, or created by the agent).

POST /organizations/{id}/notes.abuse: Same directory rule as users (user.dir, or an organization on a visible ticket, or created by the agent).

PUT /organizations/{id}.abuse: Rename with base value; duplicate names are refused as candidates. Needs org.edit.

PATCH /organizations/{id}/profile.abuse: Account manager, domain mapping and primary contacts only, with org.edit + base value. `sharing` and the collaborator/assignment flags are NOT editable (PC-S4, MSOLIS 2026-09-28): typed 422 `not_editable`; they are still read and preserved on save.

PATCH /organizations/{id}/extra.abuse: Real CAS on the raw text; only the BCW line is touched.

GET /match/contact.abuse: Candidate lookups need the value being looked up; contact/organization matches are charged to the lookup budget; org-by-id answers only for organizations the agent may read.

GET /match/organization.abuse: Candidate lookups need the value being looked up; contact/organization matches are charged to the lookup budget; org-by-id answers only for organizations the agent may read.

GET /match/ticket.abuse: Candidate lookups need the value being looked up; contact/organization matches are charged to the lookup budget; org-by-id answers only for organizations the agent may read.

GET /sync/organizations.abuse: Bulk copy of every contact/organization: now requires user.dir (was open to any agent).

GET /reports/support.abuse: Aggregates over the agent's visible tickets only.

GET /knowledge/categories.abuse: Any logged-in agent reads every article/category, as the SCP does (no per-article ACL in the core); no notes, attachments or writes; answer HTML sanitized by the core.

GET /knowledge/articles.abuse: Any logged-in agent reads every article/category, as the SCP does (no per-article ACL in the core); no notes, attachments or writes; answer HTML sanitized by the core. `q` 2-100 chars, limit <=100.

GET /knowledge/articles/{id}.abuse: Any logged-in agent reads every article/category, as the SCP does (no per-article ACL in the core); no notes, attachments or writes; answer HTML sanitized by the core.

GET /lists.consumer: custom lists catalogs: equipment (modules 7, 8), Service Orders FE.4, Quotes catalog, ticket field Equipo (OW-REQ-63)
GET /lists.abuse: Any logged-in agent reads every custom list (the installed base is visible to every agent, EQ-D3); typed core lists excluded; no notes, masks or writes; reading never creates the property form. limit<=500.

GET /lists/roles.abuse: Authenticated agents receive only the installation-scoped configured role identity; no list enumeration, names, configuration or secrets. Missing/invalid configuration returns 503 not_configured.

GET /lists/{id}/items.consumer: custom lists catalogs: equipment (modules 7, 8), Service Orders FE.4, Quotes catalog, ticket field Equipo (OW-REQ-63)
GET /lists/{id}/items.abuse: Same exposure as /lists; `q` 2-100 chars (core search predicate); retired items only with include_disabled=1; properties by logical name; version = hash of the whole list. No writes.

GET /maintenances.abuse: Any logged-in agent reads every maintenance (no customer data, no secrets; equipment ids and dates only). Incremental cursor by (updated_at, id); limit<=200; filters equipment_id / ticket_id.

GET /maintenances/{uuid}.abuse: Same exposure as the list; 404 for an unknown id.

POST /maintenances/batch.abuse: anydept.ticket.create. Max 200 items; each id inserted at most once (client uuid) and (equipment, date) unique among non-cancelled; equipment must be an ENABLED item of the configured Installed Equipment list. Worst case: junk PLANNED rows that a manager cancels.

POST /maintenances/{uuid}/reschedule.reversible: yes (base value; old date kept in changes[])
POST /maintenances/{uuid}/reschedule.abuse: anydept.ticket.create; PLANNED only; base = date seen, mandatory reason, uniqueness enforced by the database; append-only audit.

POST /maintenances/{uuid}/complete.reversible: yes (manager revert; values kept in changes[])
POST /maintenances/{uuid}/complete.abuse: anydept.ticket.create; PLANNED only; completed_on never in the future; evidence_ref must be a published document of the linked Ticket or a completion_note is required; base = status seen.

POST /maintenances/{uuid}/cancel.reversible: partial (no delete; a cancelled record is never re-opened: a new one is created)
POST /maintenances/{uuid}/cancel.abuse: Administrator or manager of ANY department only; PLANNED only; mandatory reason; the row is kept with its audit; base = status seen.

POST /maintenances/{uuid}/revert.reversible: yes (complete again; previous values kept in changes[])
POST /maintenances/{uuid}/revert.abuse: Administrator or manager of ANY department only; COMPLETED to PLANNED; mandatory reason; completion fields are cleared but preserved in the audit entry.

POST /maintenances/{uuid}/link.abuse: anydept.ticket.create AND ticket.view on the target Ticket (403 for both missing and inaccessible: no probing); PLANNED without Ticket only; base = ticket_id seen.

POST /maintenances/{uuid}/unlink.abuse: anydept.ticket.create; needs no access to the Ticket (an inaccessible Ticket must not trap the record); mandatory reason; PLANNED only; base = ticket_id seen.

GET /contracts.abuse: Feed of the contracts the agent may read: Admin or manager of ANY department read all; the rest only the organizations they may read (user.dir, an organization on a Ticket they see, or created by them). Ids only (no organization names); drafts, hashes and PDF metadata beyond title/role/state/date are manager-only. Incremental cursor by (updated_at, id), not paginated (MAY LATER); per-agent ETag; carries the installation time zone.

POST /contracts.reversible: partial (no delete; a draft is discarded and the contract voided, never removed)
POST /contracts.abuse: Administrator or manager of ANY department only. Creates a DRAFT contract and its first draft version for an existing organization; the organization never changes; contract number unique per organization (database key). Worst case: junk drafts that a manager discards (kept, VOIDED).

GET /contracts/entitlement.abuse: Resolution of the entitlement (nine outcomes) as of a date or instant; nothing is stored. Read authorization over the evaluation organization (equipment's current owner, else the organization sent) - 403 otherwise. ORG_MISMATCH reveals no contract of the other organization.

GET /contracts/catalogs.abuse: Any logged-in agent: classification catalog versions hold only codes, labels and a treatment (no customer or commercial data). Small, immutable, numbered.

POST /contracts/catalogs.reversible: n/a (a catalog version is immutable; a new version supersedes it)
POST /contracts/catalogs.abuse: Administrator or manager of ANY department only; base = latest catalog number (unique key, no lost publish); mandatory reason; max 200 codes.

GET /contracts/{uuid}.abuse: Admin/manager of ANY department, or authorization to read the contract's organization; the same 404 for unknown and not-yours (no probing). Readers get existence, display title, role, state and date of documents (no URL, path, hash, size or author) and no drafts.

PATCH /contracts/{uuid}.reversible: yes (old title/number kept in the HEADER_EDITED event)
PATCH /contracts/{uuid}.abuse: Administrator or manager of ANY department only; header (title, number) only, never terms; base = contract rev; mandatory reason; before/after kept in the append-only event.

GET /contracts/{uuid}/events.abuse: Same read authorization as the contract; append-only history (kind, actor, server time, reason); no hash or file data in document events. limit<=200, cursor = seq.

PUT /contracts/{uuid}/draft.reversible: yes (the draft is mutable until activation; discard keeps it)
PUT /contracts/{uuid}/draft.abuse: Administrator or manager of ANY department only. Creates or replaces the ONE open draft (UNIQUE contract + open_draft); an EFFECTIVE version can never be written by this route (UPDATE guarded by status=DRAFT); base = draft rev.

POST /contracts/{uuid}/draft/discard.reversible: partial (the draft is kept DISCARDED; a never-activated contract becomes VOIDED, terminal)
POST /contracts/{uuid}/draft/discard.abuse: Administrator or manager of ANY department only; mandatory reason; base = draft rev; nothing is deleted.

POST /contracts/{uuid}/activate.reversible: partial (an EFFECTIVE version is immutable; undone only by VOID or a CORRECTION, both audited)
POST /contracts/{uuid}/activate.abuse: Administrator or manager of ANY department only. One transaction serialized per organization (all its contract rows locked): revalidates completeness, equipment (Installed list, ACTIVE, owner), I1-I8 and the overlap rule over the whole organization; base = the REVIEWED draft rev; mandatory reason; computes terms_hash (sha256).

PUT /contracts/{uuid}/termination.abuse: Administrator or manager of ANY department only; terminated_on (first day without coverage) or null to revoke; revoking revalidates overlaps under the organization lock; mandatory reason; base = contract rev; terms are never touched.

POST /contracts/{uuid}/versions/{version.reversible: no (VOIDED is terminal; a correction is a new version)
POST /contracts/{uuid}/versions/{version.abuse: Administrator or manager of ANY department only; EFFECTIVE -> VOIDED without replacement (the row and its hash are kept); the only EFFECTIVE version voids the contract; revalidates overlaps; mandatory reason; base = contract rev.

POST /contracts/{uuid}/versions/{version.reversible: partial (documents are never removed; replacing marks the old one SUPERSEDED)
POST /contracts/{uuid}/versions/{version.abuse: Administrator or manager of ANY department only. file_id must be a PDF (%PDF- header, detected type) the same agent uploaded with POST /files; linked durably through a core attachment row (immune to the orphan cleanup); display_title is controlled (never the file name or an amount); DRAFT/EFFECTIVE versions only; mandatory reason; base = contract rev.

GET /contracts/{uuid}/documents/{doc_uui.abuse: Administrator or manager of ANY department only (the PDF can carry prices); readers never receive a URL, path or hash. nosniff, CSP sandbox, attachment disposition, ETag = sha256.

GET /tickets/{id}/entitlement-bases.abuse: ticket.view on the consumer Ticket; the immutable decision bases of that Ticket (result, version, hash, snapshot of the policy, what the user saw).

POST /tickets/{id}/entitlement-bases.reversible: n/a (immutable; a reclassification is a new basis that supersedes)
POST /tickets/{id}/entitlement-bases.abuse: ticket.edit on the consumer Ticket. The server resolves the entitlement itself (as_of = the Ticket's time, evaluation organization from the equipment, policy copied from the resolved version); client-sent results are ignored; base = latest basis id (unique chain link, a race answers 409).

Redundant with PUT /users/{id}/organization (base-checked); changes who sees organization-shared tickets; no consumer.
Same as above (org_id:null removes the organization).

No consumer designed; `signature` is appended to customer e-mails (phishing vector for a stolen token) and `on_vacation` disables assignment. Re-introduce only if the Configuration module demonstrates the need, without `signature`.
PC-S1 (MSOLIS 2026-09-28): moves the whole conversation and portal access to another contact; no approved consumer. Reopen only through UX requirement -> demonstrated gap -> OW-REQ -> review.
